In the following question, correct the equation by interchanging the two signs.

6 ÷ 17 × 51 + 6 - 12 = -4
questions.solution:
On interchanging,

1) × and ÷ → 6 × 17 ÷ 51 + 6 – 12 = -4

2) + and ÷ → 6 + 17 × 51 ÷ 6 - 12 = 138.5

3) + and - → 6 ÷ 17 × 51 - 6 + 12 = 24

4) – and ÷ → 6 - 17 × 51 + 6 ÷ 12 = -861.5

Hence, × and ÷ should be interchange.

questions.question: Which amongst the following is not a component of monetary policy in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which amongst the following is not a component of monetary policy in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Public Debt

  • Public Debt (Government Debt) is the debt owed by the government.
  • Whereas monetary policy is framed, devised, and implemented by the RBI.
  • Public Debt does not fall in the ambit of RBI and can never be a part of monetary policy.
  • Public debt includes the total liabilities of the Union government that have to be paid from the Consolidated Fund of India. Sometimes, the term is also used to refer to the overall liabilities of the central and state governments. However, the Union government clearly distinguishes its debt liabilities from those of the states. It calls the overall liabilities of both the Union government and states as General Government Debt (GGD) or Consolidated General Government Debt.
  • Since the Union government relies heavily on market borrowing to meet its operational and developmental expenditure, the study of public debt becomes key to understand the financial health of the government. The study of public debt involves the study of various factors such as debt-to-GDP ratio, and sustainability, and sources of government debt. The fact that almost a fourth of the government expenditure goes into interest payment explains the magnitude of the liabilities of the Union government.

questions.solution:
• Bardoli Satyagraha was started in 1928 in the state of Gujarat during the period of British Raj lead by SardarVallabhBhaipatel
  • The movement was started to reduce the taxes for the year in face of the calamities. Patel then instructed all the farmers of Bardolitaluka to refuse payment of their taxes.

  • He directed them that the struggle would not end only by the cancellation of all taxes for the year, but when all the seized property and lands were returned to their rightful owners.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
questions.questionHtml: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

Key Points 

  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak raised the slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!”.
  • The word Swarajya was first coined by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak was also known as Lokmanya Tilak.
  • He established a prominent organization Deccan Education Society to promote modern learning.
  • He also established Fergusson College at Pune.
  • He along with Annie Besant played an important role during Home Rule Movement(1916-18).
  • Kesari and Mahratta were the two newspapers started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

Important Points

  • Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel popularly known as Sardar Patel was an Indian statesman.
  • He served as the First Deputy Prime Minister of India.
  • He was an Indian barrister and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress who played a leading role in the country's struggle for independence and guided its integration into a united, independent nation. 
  • His commitment to national integration in the newly independent country was total and uncompromising, earning him the sobriquet "Iron Man of India".

  • Subhash Chandra Bose, a Freedom Fighter addressed Mahatma Gandhi as "Father of the Nation" for the 1st time.

  • Mahatma Gandhiji is revered in India as the Father of the Nation.
  • Much before the Constitution of Free India conferred the title of the Father of the Nation upon the Mahatma, it was Bose who first addressed him as such in his condolence message to the Mahatma on the demise of Kasturba Gandhi.

Last number divisible by 3 but less than 200 is 3 × 66 = 198

⇒ Total numbers = 66 – 1 + 1 = 66 numbers

But this includes the number which is divisible by 7 also

Since we know that LM of 3 and 7 is 21

So, the first 1st number divisible by 21 is 21 × 1 = 21

Last number divisible by 21 but less than 200 is 21 × 9 = 189

⇒ Total numbers = 9 – 1 + 1 = 9 numbers

⇒ (x + 5)2 + [1/(x + 5)2] = (4 + 5 )2 – 2 = 79

∴ (x + 5)2 + [1/(x + 5)2] is 79

⇒ a + 1/a = 9

⇒ a2 + 1/a2 + 2 = 81

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence given with blank is to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. The elephant stampeded and tore _____ the streets.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, the sentence given with blank is to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. 

The elephant stampeded and tore _____ the streets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. 'Down'.

Key Points

  • In this context, "down" is the appropriate preposition to use with the verb "tore" (past of "tear").
  • "Tore down" is a phrasal verb which means to destroy or remove something in a forceful and often reckless manner.
  • The sentence suggests that the elephant was in a state of stampede and was destructively running through the streets.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'The elephant stampeded and tore down the streets.'

Additional Information

  • Here's the explanation for the other options:
    • On - "Tore on" doesn't make sense in this context. "On" could be used with verbs like "ran" or "rushed" ("The elephant ran on the streets"), but not with "tore".
    • Out - "Tore out" typically means to remove something quickly or violently, often from a book or a piece of paper. It doesn't fit well with the action of an elephant running through the streets.
    • Off - "Tore off" means to remove something quickly or violently, like tearing off a piece of cloth. It also doesn't fit well in this context.

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. P: And the victims are likely to be the poorest of the poor as well as the very sources of water- rivers, wetlands and aquifers. Q: In India, water conflicts are likely to worsen before they begin to be resolved. R: Till then they pose a significant threat to economic growth, security and health of the ecosystem. S: Water is radically altering and affecting political boundaries all over world, between as well as within countries.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P: And the victims are likely to be the poorest of the poor as well as the very sources of water- rivers, wetlands and aquifers.

Q: In India, water conflicts are likely to worsen before they begin to be resolved.

R: Till then they pose a significant threat to economic growth, security and health of the ecosystem.

S: Water is radically altering and affecting political boundaries all over world, between as well as within countries.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: SQPR

The sentences talk about water conflicts and the threats they pose. Therefore, the opening sentence of the passage must introduce the concept of water conflicts, which is done only by Sentence S. Moreover, Sentence P begins with an ‘and’, and cannot start a passage. Hence, the correct answer is SQPR.

Q: This invariably acts as an incentive for outsources to be lax in developing the business. R: Despite being the dominant partner in the relationship, the outsourcer doesn't always have all the advantages. S: The trade refers to it as the minimum guarantee clause, which means that if an outsource is unable to reach an anticipated sales level, he will be compensated for the balance amount.
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

P: For one, very few entrepreneurs are willing to take on a new outsourcer, unless it comes with a guarantee of a certain level of sales.

Q: This invariably acts as an incentive for outsources to be lax in developing the business.

R: Despite being the dominant partner in the relationship, the outsourcer doesn't always have all the advantages.

S: The trade refers to it as the minimum guarantee clause, which means that if an outsource is unable to reach an anticipated sales level, he will be compensated for the balance amount.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: RPSQ

The sentences talk about sales and outsourcer. Therefore, the opening sentence of the passage must introduce the concept of ‘outsourcer’.

When reading Sentence S, it consists of an ‘it’, which refers to something else and can’t be the opening sentence.

Sentence Q uses ‘this’, which is a reference.

Sentence P uses ‘for one’, as a reason for something and has a reference.

Therefore, only Sentence R is free of references and is the opening sentence. Hence, the correct answer is RPSQ.
